label: accounting system
definition: The contractor's system for recording and reporting costs that the DFARS accounting system criteria test.
boundary_rule: One of the business systems; not the ERP product.

label: actual cost of work performed
definition: The cost actually incurred and recorded for the work completed in a period.
boundary_rule: Not the invoice amount, and not earned value.

label: actual indirect rate
definition: An indirect rate computed from the costs actually recorded in a period, before audit and before final settlement.
boundary_rule: Not the provisional billing rate (an estimate used to bill), the forward pricing rate (a projection) or the final rate (settled).

label: adjusted EBITDA
definition: EBITDA after further adjustments that the preparer selects for items it treats as unusual or non-operating.
boundary_rule: A non-GAAP measure with no standard definition, so not comparable across preparers unless the adjustments match. Not EBITDA and not cash flow.

label: administrative contracting officer
definition: The contracting officer who administers contracts after award, including rates and business systems.
boundary_rule: A role, not necessarily a separate person: a single contracting officer may be responsible for both awarding and administering a contract.

label: Allocability
definition: Assignment of a cost to objectives based on benefit or an equitable relationship.
boundary_rule: An allocable cost is not necessarily allowable.

label: Allocation Base
definition: The measure (e.g., direct labor hours, total cost input) that represents the benefit or causation for allocating indirect costs from a pool to cost objectives.
boundary_rule: Must not be confused with the cost pool itself or a simple denominator; it must demonstrate a causal or beneficial relationship.

label: Allowability
definition: Assessment of whether a cost is permitted under the applicable contract and cost principles.
boundary_rule: Allocability and reasonableness alone do not settle every allowability condition.

label: Applicability record
definition: A controlled record linking an obligation to the governing instrument and the evidence supporting its application.
boundary_rule: A public announcement does not replace the executed contract.

label: Backlog Waterfall
definition: A reconciliation showing opening backlog plus bookings plus modifications minus cancellations minus revenue equals ending backlog.
boundary_rule: Must not be confused with a simple backlog balance; it explains the change.

label: Basis of Estimate
definition: A documented narrative explaining the method, scope, quantities, assumptions, source evidence, and calculations behind a specific estimate line.
boundary_rule: Must not be confused with the estimate number itself or a simple assumption log; it is the supporting documentation.

label: bid and proposal cost
definition: The cost of preparing, submitting and supporting bids and proposals that is not required by a contract.
boundary_rule: Not IR&D. A proposal a contract requires is a direct cost of that contract.

label: Billing
definition: A request for payment prepared under the contract payment terms.
boundary_rule: An invoice or voucher does not by itself establish revenue or cash receipt.

label: book-to-bill ratio
definition: Bookings in a period divided by revenue in the same period; above 1 means orders came in faster than revenue was earned.
boundary_rule: A flow ratio for one period, not the backlog balance. State whether the denominator is revenue or billings and whether bookings include options.

label: Booked Backlog
definition: The remaining value of firm orders expected to become revenue under the company's accounting definition, excluding unexercised options and IDIQ ceilings.
boundary_rule: Must not be confused with total contract value, IDIQ ceiling, or pipeline; it is firm, booked work.

label: bookings
definition: The value of firm orders and awards received in a period, counted under the company's booking policy.
boundary_rule: Not revenue, billings or cash. An unexercised option or an IDIQ ceiling is not a booking until an order or an exercise makes it firm.

label: budget at completion
definition: The total budget for the work, the sum of all budgets allocated to it.
boundary_rule: A budget, not a forecast. The forecast is the estimate at completion.

label: Capacity Status Ladder
definition: A granular classification of production capacity status, ranging from announced and funded to operational and observed output, preventing the collapse of distinct stages into a single number.
boundary_rule: Must not be confused with a single 'capacity' figure; it distinguishes between potential, construction, and actual output.

label: Capital in progress
definition: Costs accumulated for an asset before it meets the applicable ready-for-use criteria.
boundary_rule: Payment, ownership and readiness for use are separate determinations.

label: CAS coverage
definition: Whether, and how fully, the Cost Accounting Standards apply to a contract or a business unit: full coverage, modified coverage or exempt.
boundary_rule: Coverage is decided per contract and business unit at award, not per company once. Thresholds are claims, not part of this definition.

label: Cash receipt
definition: A receipt of funds recorded against an identified payment obligation.
boundary_rule: Do not treat a submitted or accepted invoice as collected cash.

label: certified cost or pricing data
definition: Cost or pricing data that the offeror certifies as accurate, complete and current as of the date of price agreement, when the law requires it.
boundary_rule: Not data other than certified cost or pricing data. Whether certification is required is a threshold and exception question held in claims.

label: class deviation
definition: Agency authority to depart from the codified FAR or a supplement for a class of contract actions, until it is rescinded or written into the regulation.
boundary_rule: Not a final rule. For DoD under the overhaul the deviation text, not the codified part, may be what applies.

label: Close reconciliation
definition: A documented comparison of a ledger balance with independent support and the disposition of differences.
boundary_rule: A balance comparison without explanations and review is incomplete.

label: cognizant federal agency
definition: The agency that, for a contractor, is responsible for establishing forward pricing rates, final indirect cost rates and administering CAS.
boundary_rule: An agency role, not a person.

label: commercial and government entity code
definition: An identifier that the Defense Logistics Agency assigns to identify a commercial or government entity by unique location; NATO members assign the equivalent NCAGE code outside the United States.
boundary_rule: Identifies an entity at a location, so one entity can hold several codes. Not the unique entity identifier (UEI), which identifies the entity itself.

label: commercial product
definition: A product of a type customarily used by the general public or non-government entities and sold, leased or offered to the general public, with the variants the definition allows.
boundary_rule: Commercial status is decided per item and per acquisition; it is not a company attribute.

label: Company calibration
definition: Confirmation of how a general term, method or obligation applies in the actual organization.
boundary_rule: Public support does not imply company approval.

label: Consequential claim
definition: A statement whose use can materially affect a financial, contractual or control decision.
boundary_rule: Drafting, verification, applicability and adoption are independent judgments.

label: Contract asset
definition: A right to consideration that remains conditional on something beyond the passage of time.
boundary_rule: Keep distinct from a receivable and from physical inventory.

label: contract ceiling
definition: The most the Government may be required to pay or order under a contract: a ceiling price on a priced contract, or the maximum quantity or value of an indefinite-delivery contract.
boundary_rule: A cap, not funding and not expected revenue. An IDIQ ceiling is not backlog, and funded value, not the ceiling, caps a cost-type obligation.

label: Contract financing
definition: A payment arrangement supporting contract performance before ordinary payment for delivered items or services.
boundary_rule: Distinguish financing payments from delivery payments and recognized revenue.

label: Contract liability
definition: An obligation to transfer goods or services for consideration already received or due under the applicable accounting policy.
boundary_rule: Customer billing or cash can precede revenue.

label: contract line item number
definition: The number that identifies a separately listed supply or service line in a contract schedule, assigned under the DFARS uniform numbering system.
boundary_rule: Numbers a line, not the contract: the PIID identifies the contract or order. Not an accounting classification reference number (ACRN), which links a line to accounting data.

label: contractor business systems
definition: The DoD set of contractor systems subject to review and payment withholds on CAS-covered contracts that include each system's clause: accounting, estimating, purchasing, earned value management, material management and accounting, and property management.
boundary_rule: Each system has its own clause and criteria; approval of one says nothing about another.

label: control account
definition: The management point where scope, budget, actual cost and schedule meet and performance is measured.
boundary_rule: Above work packages; not a ledger account.

label: Control evidence
definition: A retained artifact showing how a control operated for a specified event or period.
boundary_rule: A written policy describes a control but does not prove operation.

label: cost accounting practice
definition: A disclosed or established method of measuring cost, assigning it to periods or allocating it to cost objectives.
boundary_rule: A change in a practice is a CAS event with its own process; a change in estimates is not.

label: Cost Accounting Standards
definition: The standards issued by the Cost Accounting Standards Board that govern how covered contractors measure, assign and allocate costs to contracts.
boundary_rule: CAS rules how cost is measured and assigned; the FAR cost principles rule whether it is allowable. Not GAAP.

label: cost analysis
definition: Reviewing the separate cost elements and profit or fee of a proposal, and the judgements behind them, to determine a fair and reasonable price or cost realism.
boundary_rule: Cost analysis may be used to determine cost realism; cost realism analysis asks whether proposed costs fit the proposed work.

label: Cost-Estimating Relationship
definition: A parametric relationship between cost and a physical or functional driver, used to generate estimates based on historical data and statistical analysis.
boundary_rule: Must not be confused with a simple unit price or a learning curve; it is a specific parametric model.

label: cost objective
definition: A function, organisational unit, contract or other work unit for which cost data are collected and measured.
boundary_rule: A final cost objective, such as a contract, receives allocations and is not allocated onward; an intermediate one is.

label: cost or pricing data
definition: All facts a prudent buyer or seller would reasonably expect to affect price negotiations significantly, as of the date of price agreement.
boundary_rule: Facts, not judgement; judgement is not cost or pricing data, though the facts under it are.

label: cost performance index
definition: Earned value divided by actual cost: the budget value earned per unit of cost spent.
boundary_rule: Measures cost efficiency only; schedule efficiency is the SPI.

label: Cost Pool
definition: A logical grouping of indirect costs that share a common allocation base, serving as the numerator in the rate calculation.
boundary_rule: Must not be confused with a general ledger account or a department; it is a specific accounting construct for allocation.

label: cost realism analysis
definition: Reviewing a proposal's cost elements to judge whether they are realistic for the work, reflect an understanding of it and match the technical approach.
boundary_rule: Used to adjust probable cost on cost-type awards, not to set a fixed price.

label: data other than certified cost or pricing data
definition: Pricing data, cost data or judgemental information a contracting officer needs to determine a fair and reasonable price or cost realism, without the certification.
boundary_rule: Carries no certificate and no defective pricing remedy.

label: Decision right
definition: An explicitly assigned authority to propose, review, approve or execute a defined decision.
boundary_rule: Task ownership alone does not grant approval authority.

label: defective pricing
definition: Certified cost or pricing data that were not accurate, complete or current as of the date of price agreement and increased the price by a significant amount, giving the government a right to reduce the price.
boundary_rule: Not a pricing error found before agreement, and not a mischarge of cost.

label: Defense Contract Audit Agency
definition: The DoD agency that audits contractors and advises contracting officers on cost and price.
boundary_rule: An adviser to contracting officers; it does not award contracts, though under the auditor determination procedure its auditors may establish final indirect cost rates.

label: Defense Contract Management Agency
definition: The DoD agency that administers many DoD contracts after award.
boundary_rule: Administers; it is not the audit agency.

label: Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement
definition: The DoD supplement to the FAR, codified at 48 CFR chapter 2, with procedures, guidance and information in a companion PGI.
boundary_rule: The PGI is guidance, not regulation.

label: Defense Production Act Title III
definition: The part of the Defense Production Act that authorizes Government assistance to expand production capacity and supply of industrial resources essential to national defense.
boundary_rule: An assistance authority, not an ordinary procurement and not the priorities and allocations system (DPAS). Testing and qualification of resources developed with it are governed by FAR subpart 34.1 and clause 52.234-1.

label: direct cost
definition: A cost identified specifically with one final cost objective, such as one contract.
boundary_rule: The test is identification with one objective, not the type of cost. A cost charged direct on one contract must not also sit in an indirect pool.

label: Disclosure Statement
definition: The form on which a covered contractor describes its cost accounting practices, filed where the CAS rules require it.
boundary_rule: Not the estimating system description or the accounting manual.

label: earned value
definition: The budget value of the work actually completed.
boundary_rule: Not actual cost. It is measured in budget, not spend.

label: earned value management system
definition: A management system that integrates scope, schedule and cost to measure progress against a time-phased plan.
boundary_rule: A system the contractor runs, not a report. Applicability by contract value is a claim.

label: EBITDA
definition: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization: a non-GAAP measure of operating earnings.
boundary_rule: Not net income, operating income or cash flow. A filed non-GAAP measure is shown with the most directly comparable GAAP measure, with equal or greater prominence, and a reconciliation to it.
aliases: earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization

label: Enterprise value
definition: Value of the operating business under an explicitly stated transaction valuation convention.
boundary_rule: Bridge separately to equity value using the agreed debt, cash and other adjustments.

label: Entity Resolution Ladder
definition: A hierarchical process for matching supplier entities, starting with exact identifiers (UEI/CAGE), then authoritative crosswalks, then fuzzy matching, with human confirmation for conflicts.
boundary_rule: Must not be confused with simple name matching; it prioritizes authoritative identifiers over fuzzy logic.

label: Estimate at Completion
definition: The total forecast cost of the project, calculated as actual cost to date plus estimate to complete, distinct from the baseline budget.
boundary_rule: Must not be confused with BAC or the original budget; it is the current expectation.

label: Estimate Snapshot
definition: An immutable package containing the estimate model, basis of estimates, source manifest, and approvals, preserved to allow for future reconstruction and audit.
boundary_rule: Must not be confused with a live working file or a versioned spreadsheet; it is a frozen, auditable record.

label: Estimate to Complete
definition: The realistic forecast cost of the remaining authorized work, built from bottom-up estimates of remaining hours, materials, and indirects.
boundary_rule: Must not be confused with 'budget left' or simple remaining budget; it is a forward-looking estimate.

label: Estimating System
definition: The contractor's policies, procedures and practices for budgeting and planning controls and for generating cost estimates for proposals, including its organization, internal controls and estimating methods.
boundary_rule: Must not be confused with a single estimate or a spreadsheet; it is the overarching system and methodology.

label: Evidence lineage
definition: The chain linking a statement or output to its source version, locator and transformations.
boundary_rule: Repeated reports from one underlying source do not establish independent corroboration.

label: expressly unallowable cost
definition: A cost that a law, regulation or contract term names as unallowable in so many words.
boundary_rule: Narrower than unallowable cost. Including one in a final indirect cost rate proposal draws a penalty; including a cost already determined unallowable for that contractor draws a penalty of twice the amount.

label: facilities capital cost of money
definition: An imputed cost of the capital tied up in facilities, computed under the cost principle and CAS rules.
boundary_rule: An imputed cost, not interest; interest stays unallowable.

label: Federal Acquisition Regulation
definition: The primary regulation for acquisitions by executive agencies, codified at 48 CFR chapter 1.
boundary_rule: Not the DFARS, which supplements it for DoD, and not the CAS, which is chapter 99.

label: Final Indirect Rate
definition: The actual allowable and allocable fiscal-year pool divided by the actual fiscal-year base, settled via the final indirect-cost-rate proposal.
boundary_rule: Must not be confused with provisional rates or forward rates; it is the rate established and agreed by the Government and the contractor as not subject to change.

label: Forecast Vintage
definition: An immutable stored version of a forecast, kept to measure accuracy by horizon and track what changed between versions.
boundary_rule: Must not be confused with the current live forecast; it is a historical snapshot.

label: forward pricing rate agreement
definition: A written agreement between the contractor and the government on rates for pricing contracts over a period.
boundary_rule: Not a recommendation and not a billing rate. It makes rates available for pricing in the period it names, and either party may cancel it.

label: forward pricing rate recommendation
definition: A rate set unilaterally by the administrative contracting officer for Government use in negotiations or other contract actions when forward pricing rate agreement negotiations are not complete or the contractor will not agree to one.
boundary_rule: Not an agreement; the contractor has not agreed to it.

label: fringe benefits
definition: Allowances and services a contractor provides employees as compensation in addition to regular wages and salaries, such as vacation, sick leave, holidays and insurance, usually pooled and applied to labour.
boundary_rule: A pool in its own right at some companies and part of overhead at others.

label: Funded Backlog
definition: Firm orders that have authorized and appropriated funding, distinct from unfunded backlog.
boundary_rule: Must not be confused with total backlog or unfunded backlog; it is specifically funded work.

label: Funding
definition: Amount made available under the relevant funding instrument.
boundary_rule: Separate from contract ceiling, billings, revenue and cash.

label: general and administrative expense
definition: A management, financial or other expense incurred for the general management and administration of the business unit as a whole.
boundary_rule: Not overhead. Its base under CAS is a cost input base.

label: government-owned contractor-operated plant
definition: A plant or facility that the Government owns and a contractor operates under contract.
boundary_rule: Ownership and operation are split: not a contractor-owned plant and not a Government-owned, Government-operated (GOGO) facility. Some GOCO plants belong to the organic industrial base.

label: home office
definition: An office responsible for directing or managing two or more segments of an organisation, whose costs are allocated to them.
boundary_rule: Allocation of its costs follows CAS rules for covered contracts.

label: hurdle rate
definition: The minimum expected return that a proposed investment must clear to be approved.
boundary_rule: A decision threshold set by policy, usually the cost of capital plus a premium. Not the expected return of the project and not a realized return.
aliases: required return|minimum acceptable rate of return

label: incurred cost submission
definition: The contractor's annual proposal of final indirect cost rates for a fiscal year, with supporting schedules.
boundary_rule: Not an audit; an audit may follow it. Its due date is a claim.
aliases: ICS|final indirect cost rate proposal|incurred cost proposal

label: independent estimate at completion
definition: An estimate at completion calculated from performance data by someone other than the contractor, typically actual cost plus the remaining budgeted work divided by the cost performance index.
boundary_rule: A check on the contractor's estimate at completion, not that estimate and not a budget. State the efficiency index it assumes.

label: independent research and development
definition: Contractor-initiated technical effort that is not sponsored by, or required in performance of, a contract or grant.
boundary_rule: Not bid and proposal cost, though the two share a cost principle.

label: indirect cost
definition: A cost that serves more than one final cost objective, or an intermediate one, and is assigned through a pool and an allocation base.
boundary_rule: Not overhead alone: G&A, fringe and other pools are indirect too. Not unallowable by nature.

label: Industrial Base Analysis and Sustainment
definition: A Department of Defense program that funds projects to sustain and strengthen the industrial base capabilities and supply chains that defense systems depend on.
boundary_rule: A program that makes awards, not a statute. Separate from DPA Title III, an authority with its own funding; an award under one is not an award under the other.

label: Inventory work in process
definition: Production costs carried as inventory under the applicable accounting policy.
boundary_rule: Physical work in process and contract work performed can have different accounting treatment.

label: Investment stage gate
definition: A defined review at which evidence supports continuing, revising or stopping an investment.
boundary_rule: An approved budget does not eliminate later delivery or benefit checks.

label: Issue and action log
definition: A record connecting an issue to its decision owner, next action, due condition and closure evidence.
boundary_rule: A closed task is not proof that the underlying control issue is resolved.

label: Item Identity Layer
definition: A data layer using authoritative crosswalks (NSN, part numbers, CAGE) to resolve item equivalence, preventing reliance on free-text name matching.
boundary_rule: Must not be confused with fuzzy name matching or manual aliases; it relies on authoritative identifier links.

label: labor efficiency variance
definition: The difference between actual labor hours and the standard hours allowed for the output, valued at the standard rate.
boundary_rule: Hours, not rate: the price effect is the labor rate variance. Not a learning-curve effect, though the two can overlap.

label: labor rate variance
definition: The difference between the actual and the standard hourly labor rate, multiplied by the actual hours worked.
boundary_rule: Price effect only; the hours effect is the labor efficiency variance. Not a change in an indirect rate.

label: landed cost
definition: The total cost of an item delivered to the point of use: purchase price plus freight, duty, insurance, handling and other costs of getting it there.
boundary_rule: Not the quoted unit price. Compare quotes on landed cost with the same delivery terms. Not the cost to own or use the item.

label: learning curve
definition: A model in which unit cost or hours fall by a fixed share each time cumulative quantity doubles.
boundary_rule: A model, not a fact; its slope comes from history and is an assumption.

label: limitation of cost
definition: The clause on fully funded cost-type contracts that requires notice when costs approach the estimated cost and caps the government's obligation.
boundary_rule: Applies to fully funded contracts; incrementally funded ones use limitation of funds.

label: limitation of funds
definition: The clause on incrementally funded cost-type contracts that requires notice when costs approach the funds allotted and caps the government's obligation at them.
boundary_rule: Funded value, not contract ceiling or estimated cost, is the cap.

label: management reserve
definition: Budget held outside the performance measurement baseline for unforeseen work within the contract scope.
boundary_rule: Not contingency for out-of-scope work, and not undistributed budget.

label: margin
definition: Profit expressed as a share of price: price less cost, divided by price.
boundary_rule: Not markup, which divides profit by cost: a 25% markup on cost is a 20% margin on price. Gross, operating and net margin differ by which costs are deducted.

label: markup
definition: The amount added to cost to reach price, usually stated as a percentage of cost.
boundary_rule: Not margin, which divides profit by price: a 25% markup on cost is a 20% margin. State what the markup contains: indirect cost, profit or both.

label: material management and accounting system
definition: The contractor's system for planning, controlling and accounting for material.
boundary_rule: A business system distinct from purchasing.

label: material usage variance
definition: The difference between the quantity of material actually used and the standard quantity allowed for the output, valued at the standard price.
boundary_rule: Quantity, not price: the price effect is the purchase price variance. Scrap and yield loss land here.

label: material weakness
definition: A deficiency in internal control over financial reporting severe enough that a material misstatement may not be prevented or detected in time.
boundary_rule: A financial statement audit term; the DFARS business systems clauses use the same term for information in contractor business systems.

label: net working capital
definition: Current operating assets less current operating liabilities, usually excluding cash and debt.
boundary_rule: Not the current ratio, and not a working capital peg, which is an agreed target. State whether contract assets, contract liabilities and progress payments are included.

label: nonrecurring cost
definition: A one-time cost of design, development, tooling, qualification or start-up that does not rise with the number of units built.
boundary_rule: Not a recurring unit cost. A quote or estimate must say whether it is priced separately or spread over the units.

label: nontraditional defense contractor
definition: An entity that is not currently performing, and has not performed for a set period before the solicitation, any DoD contract or subcontract subject to full CAS coverage.
boundary_rule: A status, tested at a point in time, not a size category. The period and exemptions are claims.

label: Normalized Comparable Price
definition: An observed price adjusted by index ratios, foreign exchange rates, and decomposed scope adjustments to allow for apples-to-apples comparison across different transactions.
boundary_rule: Must not be confused with raw observed prices or unadjusted quotes; it is a calculated comparative metric.

label: novation agreement
definition: An agreement by which the government recognises a successor in interest to a contract.
boundary_rule: Not a change-of-name agreement, which changes only the name.

label: organic industrial base
definition: The Government-owned depots, arsenals, shipyards and plants that perform military maintenance, repair and production; most are Government-operated and some are contractor-operated.
boundary_rule: Not the commercial defense industrial base. Ownership defines it, not who operates it: a GOCO plant can belong to it.

label: overall equipment effectiveness
definition: Availability multiplied by performance multiplied by quality for a machine or line: the share of planned production time that yields good output at the ideal rate.
boundary_rule: Not utilization, which counts running time alone, and not capacity, the maximum output. It measures how much planned time yields good parts at ideal speed.

label: overhead
definition: An indirect cost pool for costs of running operations, such as facilities and supervision, allocated to work on a base such as direct labour.
boundary_rule: Not G&A, which covers management of the business as a whole. Pool names and contents are company-specific.

label: overhead volume variance
definition: The difference between fixed overhead budgeted and fixed overhead applied to production, arising when actual activity differs from the activity level used to set the rate.
boundary_rule: Over- or under-absorption caused by volume, not by spending: a spending variance compares actual with budgeted overhead cost.

label: performance-based payment
definition: Contract financing paid when defined performance events or criteria are met.
boundary_rule: Not progress payments based on cost, and not payment for accepted items.

label: Performance Measurement Baseline
definition: The time-phased budget for authorized work, against which performance is measured, changed only by formal authorization.
boundary_rule: Must not be confused with the forecast; its summed budget is the budget at completion, and management reserve sits outside it.

label: Placed in service
definition: The point at which an asset meets the relevant ready-for-use or operating criteria under the governing policy.
boundary_rule: A purchase order or payment date does not alone determine this point.

label: planned value
definition: The time-phased budget for work scheduled to be done.
boundary_rule: Not the funds spent and not the work done.

label: Practical capacity
definition: An explicit capacity measure reflecting achievable output after specified normal operating constraints.
boundary_rule: Distinguish from nameplate, demonstrated and committed capacity.

label: price analysis
definition: Examining a proposed price without evaluating its separate cost elements and profit, mainly by comparison.
boundary_rule: Not cost analysis, which reviews the cost elements one by one.

label: Price Observation Ledger
definition: A structured table where each row represents a single piece of price evidence with its basis, quantity, scope, currency, year, and confidence, rather than a definitive unit price.
boundary_rule: Must not be confused with a final price list or a single authoritative price; it is a collection of raw observations.

label: procurement instrument identifier
definition: The Government-unique identifier for each solicitation, contract, agreement or order.
boundary_rule: Identifies the instrument, not a line in it (the CLIN) and not the contractor (the UEI). A supplementary identifier, such as an amendment number, is not unique alone.

label: progress payment
definition: Contract financing based on costs incurred as work progresses, at a customary rate, liquidated against deliveries.
boundary_rule: Based on cost, not on performance events; rates are claims.

label: Provisional Billing Rate
definition: An interim reimbursement rate used for billing costs during the contract period, intended to approximate anticipated final rates and subject to later adjustment.
boundary_rule: Must not be confused with final rates or forward estimating rates; it is a temporary billing mechanism.

label: Purchase price allocation
definition: Allocation of acquisition consideration to acquired assets and assumed liabilities under the applicable accounting framework.
boundary_rule: Transaction valuation and post-acquisition accounting answer different questions.

label: purchase price variance
definition: The difference between the actual price paid and the standard or planned price, multiplied by the quantity purchased.
boundary_rule: Price at purchase, not use: a quantity or yield effect is the material usage variance. Not escalation, which is the expected change in price over time.

label: purchasing system
definition: The contractor's system for buying and subcontracting, which a government review may approve.
boundary_rule: Not the material management system.

label: Quality of earnings
definition: Analysis of the sustainability and composition of reported earnings using traceable adjustments.
boundary_rule: An adjusted earnings measure is not cash flow or a valuation.

label: quantity break
definition: A price tier at which the unit price falls once the order quantity reaches a stated threshold.
boundary_rule: A seller's price term, not a rebate paid afterwards and not the learning-curve effect on cost. It applies to the quoted quantity and validity period only.

label: reasonable cost
definition: A cost whose nature and amount do not exceed what a prudent person in a competitive business would incur.
boundary_rule: Reasonableness is one test of allowability. A reasonable cost can still be unallowable or unallocable.

label: receivable
definition: A right to payment that is unconditional: only the passage of time is needed before payment is due.
boundary_rule: Not a contract asset (a right conditional on more than time), not revenue and not cash received.

label: Reporting cadence
definition: An agreed sequence of reporting, review and escalation events with responsible roles.
boundary_rule: A recurring meeting without an output or decision owner is not a reporting control.

label: revenue
definition: The amount recognized as earned under the company's revenue policy as performance occurs.
boundary_rule: Not bookings (ordered), billings (invoiced) or cash receipts (collected). The four differ in timing and none stands in for another.

label: Revolutionary FAR Overhaul
definition: The government-wide rewrite of the FAR into plain language with fewer non-statutory rules, issued first as model deviation text and then through rulemaking.
boundary_rule: Model deviation text binds only through an agency deviation, and a proposed rule binds nobody.

label: Rough Order of Magnitude
definition: A preliminary estimate used for early planning and screening, with its scope, assumptions, basis and uncertainty range stated.
boundary_rule: Not a firm quote or a detailed estimate; no universal accuracy range is implied.

label: schedule performance index
definition: Earned value divided by planned value: the work done as a share of the work planned.
boundary_rule: A budget-based schedule measure, not a critical path measure.

label: segment
definition: One of two or more divisions, product departments, plants or other subdivisions reporting to a home office.
boundary_rule: A cost accounting unit; not necessarily a legal entity.

label: Should-Cost Estimate
definition: A structured bottom-up estimate of what a product or service should cost based on detailed analysis of materials, labor, and overhead, independent of the supplier's quote.
boundary_rule: Must not be confused with a parametric estimate or a historical average; it is a detailed analytical construction.

label: should cost review
definition: A government review of a contractor's operations to find what a program should cost if run efficiently.
boundary_rule: Not an audit of incurred cost and not a proposal audit.

label: significant deficiency
definition: A shortcoming that materially affects reliance on a contractor business system's information; the current DFARS business systems clauses use material weakness instead.
boundary_rule: Not used in the current DFARS business systems clauses, and not the financial statement audit term of the same name.

label: Source version
definition: A uniquely identified set of source bytes retained with its provenance and hash.
boundary_rule: A changed web page is a new version even when its address stays the same.

label: supplier quote
definition: A supplier's stated offer of price and terms for a specified item, quantity and validity period.
boundary_rule: Not a purchase order, a contract price or a price actually paid. An expired or conditional quote is not an observation of market price.

label: System of record
definition: The designated authoritative source for a defined business record.
boundary_rule: A dashboard or copied workbook may only be a derived view.

label: to-complete performance index
definition: The cost efficiency the remaining work must achieve to finish at a chosen target: work remaining divided by funds remaining.
boundary_rule: Forward-looking and stated against a target (BAC or EAC), unlike the CPI, which is cost efficiency to date. Name the target with the value.

label: Tombstone Record
definition: An explicit record of a data record's deletion, withdrawal, or loss of access, ensuring that the absence of data is documented rather than silently ignored.
boundary_rule: Must not be confused with a deleted row or a null value; it is an active record of absence.

label: Truthful Cost or Pricing Data statute
definition: The statute that requires certified cost or pricing data for certain negotiated contracts and modifications and gives the government a price reduction remedy when they were defective.
boundary_rule: The statute sets the rule; the FAR and DFARS implement it. Its thresholds change by rule and live in claims.

label: unallowable cost
definition: A cost that cannot be included in prices, cost reimbursements or settlements under a government contract.
boundary_rule: Not an unallocable cost, and not every unallowable cost is expressly unallowable; the penalty rules reach expressly unallowable costs and costs already determined unallowable for the contractor.

label: unbilled receivable
definition: Consideration earned under a contract for which no invoice has yet been issued and for which only the passage of time is needed before payment is due.
boundary_rule: Not a billed receivable (invoice issued) and not a contract asset (right conditional on more than the passage of time). Regulation S-X also uses 'unbilled' for amounts not yet billable; this entry covers only amounts with an unconditional right to payment.

label: unfunded backlog
definition: Firm orders whose value exceeds the funding the customer has made available to date: work that is committed but not yet funded.
boundary_rule: Not funded backlog and not an unexercised option or IDIQ ceiling. Report it apart from funded backlog, since funding limits what may be performed and billed.

label: unique entity identifier
definition: A number or other identifier used to identify a specific commercial, nonprofit or Government entity, established through the System for Award Management.
boundary_rule: Identifies the entity, not a location: one entity can hold several CAGE codes. Not a tax identifier and not the PIID.

label: weighted guidelines
definition: The DoD structured method a contracting officer uses to develop a profit or fee objective.
boundary_rule: A government negotiating tool; it does not set the contractor's own pricing.

label: Wide Area WorkFlow
definition: The DoD electronic system in which contractors submit payment requests and receiving reports.
boundary_rule: A submission channel, not a payment: submission or acceptance there is not cash receipt. The contract and DFARS list the exceptions that allow other channels.

label: work breakdown structure
definition: A product-oriented, hierarchical breakdown of the work a program must do, in which each element carries a defined scope.
boundary_rule: Not the organizational breakdown (OBS), the schedule or a cost-element list. The control account joins the WBS and the OBS.

label: Working capital peg
definition: An agreed reference level used to calculate a transaction working capital adjustment.
boundary_rule: Specify included accounts, measurement dates and accounting conventions.

label: wrap rate
definition: A direct labour rate with all applicable indirect rates applied, used to compare or price labour quickly.
boundary_rule: A pricing shortcut, not a rate agreed with the government.
